reason: E2 directly demonstrates phase-selective recrystallization in a lamellar fcc/B2 EHEA, achieving ~35% ductility and ~2 GPa strength by fully activating strain hardening and preserving the hard phase skeleton, which supports all key premises. E1 provides context that such lamellar EHEAs can balance strength and ductility but does not address the specific intervention. The hypothesis accurately represents the cited evidence without overstatement.
premises: Phase-selective recrystallization of the soft fcc phase in a lamellar eutectic HEA is feasible via controlled heat treatment.
This recrystallization eliminates weak interphase boundaries and fully activates strain hardening in the fcc phase.
The hard B2 phase can be preserved as a continuous skeleton during recrystallization of the fcc phase.
The resulting microstructure with coherent interfaces promotes effective strain partitioning.
This microstructural modification simultaneously increases both strength and ductility compared to the as-cast state.
